stories.title: U.S. Government Pays $285M for Defense Health Agency HQ in Northern Virginia
stories.excerpt: The federal government has acquired the Defense Health Agency’s Northern Virginia headquarters for $285 million, adding another large leased office campus to the nation’s real estate portfolio. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command acquired the 44-acre property at 7700 Arlington Boulevard in Falls Church from longtime owner GBA Associates, according to property records and a General Services Administration (GSA) official cited by the Business Journals. The campus includes three Class B office buildings constructed between 1954 and 1984 with about 686,000 square feet, and a separate parcel with 2,000 parking spaces. Plans filed in 2018 called for another 179,200-square-foot office building and more parking, but that never moved forward. The Defense Health Agency, which manages health care for military and uniformed services, has occupied the campus since 2011. The agency signed a 15-year, $370 million lease in 2010. Buying the property instead of leasing is expected to save the federal government “several million dollars per year,” while supporting a broader effort to reduce federal lease obligations. The transaction follows several other large federal acquisitions of previously leased properties in the Washington region. The CIA paid $247 million in 2025 for an office it occupied in Chantilly, Va. In 2023, the federal government acquired Liberty Crossing I and II in McLean, Va., for $531 million, while the GSA paid $760 million for the Department of Transportation headquarters near the Washington Navy Yard shortly before the pandemic. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: U.S. Government purchased Defense Health Agency HQ, Falls Church VA, $285M
44-acre campus, 686K SF office, owned by GBA Associates since 2011
Federal buy-vs.-lease saves government 'several million dollars per year'
stories.summary: The federal government acquired the Defense Health Agency's Northern Virginia headquarters—a 44-acre, 686,000-square-foot Class B office campus in Falls Church—for $285 million from GBA Associates. The agency had leased the property under a 15-year, $370 million lease signed in 2010. The purchase is expected to save the government several million dollars annually while reducing federal lease obligations.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. Federal office consolidation and in-fill acquisition signals continued weak demand for suburban Class B office, confirming that prime office assets are being repurposed or deleveraged rather than traded at growth valuations. No meaningful signal for residential demand in Northern Virginia from this transaction alone.

stories.title: Distyl AI Doubles Footprint at 135 Madison Ave.
stories.excerpt: Koeppel Rosen LLC, leasing and management agent for the Rosen family portfolio, arranged a 15,038-square-foot lease expansion for Distyl AI, Inc at 135 Madison Ave. In 2025, Distyl signed a 15,038-square-foot lease for the entire 10th floor at 135 Madison. The company now occupies 30,076 square feet across two floors. Distyl AI develops AI-native operational systems for Fortune 500 and Global 2000 companies, transforming complex business knowledge into scalable, auditable workflows. Backed by leading venture firms and founded by industry veterans, Distyl AI’s expansion reflects its continued growth and commitment to advancing enterprise innovation in Manhattan. “We were pleased to work with Distyl AI to reconfigure and expand its footprint across two contiguous floors at 135 Madison Avenue. We celebrate the company’s rapidly growing operations, which required additional office space,” said Max Koeppel, Director of Leasing at Koeppel Rosen. Koeppel represented ownership, while Justin T. Pollner of Newmark negotiated for the tenant. The post Distyl AI Doubles Footprint at 135 Madison Ave. appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Distyl AI doubled NYC footprint, 135 Madison Ave., now occupies 30K SF across 2 floors
AI software company expanding operations amid strong VC backing and Fortune 500 client base
Lease expansion signals continued tech talent and office demand in Midtown Manhattan
stories.summary: Distyl AI, an AI-native operational systems company backed by leading venture firms, doubled its Manhattan office footprint by signing a second-floor lease (15,038 SF) at 135 Madison Avenue in 2025. The company now occupies 30,076 square feet across two contiguous floors. The expansion reflects rapid growth serving Fortune 500 and Global 2000 companies.
stories.impact: Tech company expansion in Midtown Manhattan signals sustained professional-services and high-salary job creation, supporting residential demand for luxury and core Upper East Side/Midtown multifamily. VC-backed software growth tends to precede white-collar migration and renter income stability; monitor whether other AI/software firms follow similar expansion patterns in Manhattan.

stories.title: Colliers Named Sale and Leasing Advisor for Oceanfront Innovation Hub
stories.excerpt: Colliers has been retained as advisor for the sale and leasing of Enclave @ Carpinteria, a three-building, 121,230-square-foot advanced manufacturing and office/flex campus located at 6303-6309 Carpinteria Ave. on the Santa Barbara South Coast. The opportunity provides owner-users and growing occupiers a rare chance to establish a large-scale coastal headquarters in one of Southern California’s most supply-constrained technology and innovation markets, according to Colliers. The assignment follows Colliers’ sale of the Tech Park @ Goleta portfolio earlier this year, a 733,497-square-foot technology campus recapitalized in a transaction reported at $235 million, the largest in Santa Barbara County history. “The success of the Tech Park @ Goleta transaction reinforced what investors already see in this market: established technology and aerospace tenants, limited supply, and growing demand from innovation-driven companies,” said vice chair Sean Fulp “Enclave represents that same thesis from an occupier perspective.” Along with Fulp, the Colliers team includes EVP Austin Herlihy of Colliers Santa Barbara, EVPs Todd Tydlaska and Mark Schuessler, VP Miles Waters, and associate VPs Jordan Garcia and Blake Hammerstein. Senior Vice President Jason Roth of Colliers’ Debt & Structured Finance will serve as financial advisor. The post Colliers Named Sale and Leasing Advisor for Oceanfront Innovation Hub appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Colliers advising on sale/lease of Enclave @ Carpinteria, Santa Barbara, 121K SF advanced manufacturing/flex
Follows $235M Tech Park @ Goleta sale (733K SF), largest Santa Barbara County transaction on record
Supply-constrained coastal tech/aerospace market attracting owner-user and growth-stage occupier interest
stories.summary: Colliers has been retained to market Enclave @ Carpinteria, a 121,230-square-foot advanced manufacturing and office/flex campus on the Santa Barbara South Coast. The assignment follows Colliers' $235 million sale of Tech Park @ Goleta (733,497 SF), the largest transaction in Santa Barbara County history. Both assets target established technology and aerospace tenants in a supply-constrained market.
stories.impact: Major institutional capital flowing into Santa Barbara County tech/aerospace real estate signals strong job-creation fundamentals and employer clustering in that coastal submarket. Multifamily developers should monitor absorption of high-wage professional tenants (aerospace, advanced manufacturing, tech) moving into Santa Barbara/Goleta; sustained corporate growth justifies new residential supply targeting 75th–90th percentile household incomes in those communities.

stories.title: Legion, SMA Equities Partner on Upper East Side Residential
stories.excerpt: Legion Investment Group, alongside SMA Equities as co-developer, completed the recapitalization of three parcels on the Upper East Side. Demolition of the existing structures on the site is already underway. “We’re closing on 201 E. 84th St., a corner assemblage that will become a new residential development on the Upper East Side,” said Victor Sigoura, founder and CEO of Legion Investment Group. “Our goal is to build on the legacy of 1122 Madison Ave. and 109 E. 79th St. (pictured) and bring our standard of quality and excellence in development to 201 East 84th Street.” Advised by Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets Institutional Advisory, led by Aaron Appel, Dustin Stolly, and Sean Bastian, Legion and SMA acquired the 201 E. 84th St. corner assemblage with a $99-million acquisition loan from BDT & MSD Partners and Deutsche Bank. They plan an approximately 300,000-square-foot residential building on Third Avenue and 84th Street. The post Legion, SMA Equities Partner on Upper East Side Residential appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Legion Investment Group & SMA Equities acquired 201 E. 84th St. assemblage, Upper East Side, $99M loan
Plans for ~300K SF residential tower on Third Ave. & 84th St.; demolition underway
Financed by BDT & MSD Partners and Deutsche Bank; Walker & Dunlop arranged capital
stories.summary: Legion Investment Group and SMA Equities closed on a corner assemblage at 201 E. 84th Street on Manhattan's Upper East Side with a $99 million acquisition loan from BDT & MSD Partners and Deutsche Bank, arranged by Walker & Dunlop. The partners plan to demolish existing structures and build an approximately 300,000-square-foot residential tower. Demolition is already underway.
stories.impact: Active land assembly and development financing on Upper East Side at scale signals continued institutional confidence in Manhattan luxury residential and strong cap-rate compression for stabilized, lease-up-ready assets. Monitor other assemblages in the UES for similar activity; sustained pre-dev financing availability suggests capital has not retreated despite macro headwinds.

stories.title: New-Construction Car Wash Properties Sell in Murrieta, Riverside
stories.excerpt: RealSource Group, a national commercial real estate brokerage company specializing in investment sales, sale‑leasebacks and tenant representation, has arranged the sale of two new-construction, single-tenant Quick Quack Car Wash properties in Murrieta and Riverside. Each property is secured by a new 20‑year absolute triple-net ground lease. The combined sales price was $8.63 million. SVP of investment sales Austin Blodgett and associate Jonathan Schiffer, CCIM, represented both sellers, two private Southern California-based developers. Located at 39480 Murrieta Hot Springs Rd., the Murrieta property sold for $4.53 million to a private international investor, represented by Dustin Lee of JK Realtage Group, Inc. The Quick Quack Car Wash located at 3605 Van Buren Blvd. in Riverside sold for $4.1 million to a private Los Angeles-based investor, who represented themselves. “Both properties generated significant interest, but the ground‑lease structure required careful buyer education,” said Blodgett. “Many express car wash investors pursue fee‑simple deals to capture bonus depreciation, so we fielded hundreds of calls explaining why these locations, tenant strength and long‑term fundamentals still make ground leases compelling. In both cases, we secured local buyers with strong Inland Empire strategies and closed well before the locations opened for business.” The post New-Construction Car Wash Properties Sell in Murrieta, Riverside appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: RealSource Group sold two Quick Quack Car Wash properties, Murrieta & Riverside CA, $8.63M combined
Each property on 20-year absolute triple-net ground lease; ground-lease structure attracted international and LA-based investors
Ground leases required 'careful buyer education' due to bonus depreciation preference for fee-simple deals
stories.summary: RealSource Group arranged the sale of two new-construction Quick Quack Car Wash properties in Murrieta (sold for $4.53M) and Riverside (sold for $4.1M) for a combined $8.63 million. Both properties are secured by 20-year absolute triple-net ground leases. The broker noted that ground-lease structure required educating buyers on long-term fundamentals over fee-simple bonus depreciation benefits.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily. Ground-lease preference for sale-leaseback single-tenant net-lease assets indicates investor preference for long-term income stability and tax efficiency in smaller markets. Not a primary signal for residential development capital flow or demand.

stories.title: Construction Firm Brasfield & Gorrie Inks 19K-SF Lease in Broward County
stories.excerpt: Construction firm Brasfield & Gorrie is relocating in South Florida, from Coral Gables to Weston, where it signed a 19,330-square-foot lease. The general contractor will move into the Weston Pointe I building in the second quarter of 2027, according to JLL, which represented the tenant. It will occupy most of the third floor within the four-story building at 2400 North Commerce Parkway, just west of I-75. It’s part of the two-building Weston Pointe campus that was built between 1999 and 2001. The move will triple Brasfield & Gorrie’s footprint from Coral Gables, where it was based within Ryder System’s former headquarters. “Brasfield & Gorrie required additional office space to accommodate their rapid growth, and Weston offered the strategic location and connectivity,” JLL’s Ryan Levy, who represented Brasfield & Gorrie, said in a statement. Cushman & Wakefield’s Chase Kulp and Deanna Lobinsky represented the landlord, New York Life Investment Management, which purchased the 99,752-square-foot asset for $114.8 million in 2016. Brasfield & Gorrie is also expanding at its headquarters in Birmingham, Ala., where it broke ground in March on a four-story, 88,000-square-foot building that will expand its existing office. The expansion is expected to cost $65 million. A representative for Brasfield & Gorrie did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Brasfield & Gorrie, major construction firm, relocating Coral Gables to Weston FL, 19.3K SF lease
Move to Weston Pointe I triples contractor's South Florida footprint; occupies Q2 2027
Reflects 'rapid growth' in regional construction activity and need for centralized operations hub
stories.summary: Construction firm Brasfield & Gorrie is relocating from Coral Gables to Weston, Florida, signing a 19,330-square-foot lease in the Weston Pointe I building. The move will triple the general contractor's footprint and take occupancy in Q2 2027. JLL represented the tenant, citing Brasfield & Gorrie's rapid growth and need for additional office space and strategic location connectivity.
stories.impact: Major regional contractor expansion and relocation to Weston signals sustained construction activity across South Florida, particularly in the western Broward County submarket. Contractor growth often lags (not leads) residential supply pipeline; this move likely reflects existing and near-term multifamily development commitments. Confirms active building environment in central/west Broward for the next 18+ months.

stories.title: Hudson Pacific Sells Nearly Vacant San Francisco Office Complex for $65M
stories.excerpt: Hudson Pacific Properties, Inc. said Friday it completed the sale of 875 and 899 Howard, two downtown San Francisco properties totaling approximately 284,000 square feet, for $65.5 million before prorations and closing costs. The buyer was not disclosed. Formerly occupied by Snapchat, 875 Howard is an approximately 188,000-square-foot office building that was 36% occupied at the time of sale, with its remaining major lease expiring next year. 899 Howard, an approximately 96,000-square-foot former retail building, was fully vacant. Hudson Pacific secured entitlements to convert two floors of 899 Howard to office use before the sale. “The sale of 875 and 899 Howard reflects our disciplined approach to recycling capital out of non-core assets,” said Victor Coleman, chairman and CEO of Hudson Pacific. “Our team’s deep understanding of San Francisco’s growing office demand guided the repositioning of 899 Howard, and the sale eliminates significant capital and re-leasing risk while enhancing our financial flexibility. We will continue executing our disposition program and driving lease-up across our portfolio.” Photo of 899 Howard courtesy of Plant Construction. The post Hudson Pacific Sells Nearly Vacant San Francisco Office Complex for $65M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Hudson Pacific sold 875 & 899 Howard, San Francisco, 284K SF, $65.5M; buyer undisclosed
875 Howard (former Snapchat HQ) only 36% occupied; 899 Howard fully vacant; major lease expiring next year
Reflects 'disciplined capital recycling' by REIT exiting non-core office assets amid weak SF office demand
stories.summary: Hudson Pacific Properties sold two downtown San Francisco office properties totaling 284,000 square feet—875 and 899 Howard—for $65.5 million. The former Snapchat headquarters (875 Howard, 188K SF) was only 36% occupied with a major lease expiring next year. The second building (899 Howard, 96K SF) was fully vacant. Hudson Pacific characterized the sale as disciplined capital recycling from non-core assets.
stories.impact: Deepening San Francisco office distress and capital flight from urban office into alternative assets (including multifamily). Ultra-low office occupancy and bulk sales of trophy-tenant space by REITs suggest sustained office headwinds will not reverse; multifamily developers in SF Bay should expect continued office-to-residential conversion entitlements and heightened competition for scarce residential land.

stories.title: Developers File Plans for 402-Unit Housing Project Along Astoria Waterfront
stories.excerpt: A pair of Astoria developers has filed plans to build 402 housing units in the World’s Borough. Dominick Acquista and Lorenzo Devardo, under the shell corporation Across the River Realty Development, filed plans to replace three industrial buildings at 31-29 Vernon Boulevard in Astoria, Queens, with a 20-story residential tower, according to city records. The New York Business Journal first reported the filing. The LLC filed plans with the New York City Planning Commission on Wednesday seeking a zoning change and text amendment to allow it to build housing above the current height restrictions. The land targeted for redevelopment sits just across Vernon Boulevard from Socrates Sculpture Park and the East River beyond that. Acquista and Devardo could not be reached for comment. Of the 402 units, about 100 of them would be affordable apartments under the city’s Mandatory Inclusionary Housing requirements for those making 60 percent of the area median income. The proposed Astoria project would also feature 10,108 square feet of commercial space and 3,069 square feet of community facility space, as well as 26 parking spaces, the application shows. Other buildings of similar size are being planned for Astoria as well. The Domain Companies secured a $175 million construction loan to build 429 units at 35-45, 35-33 and 35-42 41st Street in August. In September, Moses Freund’s Vaja Group purchased a former Staples building at 24-41 31st Street for $26 million with plans to construct a 108-unit mixed-use development. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Across the River Realty Development (Acquista/Devardo) filed Astoria, Queens plan: 402 units, 20-story tower
Site: 31-29 Vernon Blvd., replaces three industrial buildings; seeking zoning change above height limits
~100 units affordable (60% AMI); 10.1K SF commercial, 3.1K SF community facility, 26 parking
stories.summary: Developers Dominick Acquista and Lorenzo Devardo, operating as Across the River Realty Development, filed plans with NYC Planning Commission to replace three industrial buildings at 31-29 Vernon Boulevard in Astoria, Queens with a 20-story, 402-unit residential tower. Approximately 100 units would be affordable housing under Mandatory Inclusionary Housing. The project also includes 10,108 square feet of commercial space and requires a zoning change to exceed current height restrictions.
stories.impact: Astoria waterfront (Queens) residential rezoning and large-scale development filing signals institutional confidence in outer-borough residential; proximity to Socrates Sculpture Park and East River waterfront suggests strong amenity positioning. Monitor zoning approval timeline and comparable Queens projects; successful entitlement here may accelerate competing projects on or near waterfront and drive land values upward in Astoria/Long Island City submarkets.

stories.title: Legion Investment Group, SMA Equities Pair on 300K-SF UES Resi Project
stories.excerpt: Legion Investment Group and SMA Equities have teamed on a 300,000-square-foot residential development rising on Manhattan’s Upper East Side. The new partnership secured a $99 million pre-development loan for the 37-story project at 1491-1497 Third Avenue on Thursday, according to The Real Deal, which first reported the news. BDT & MSD Partners and Deutsche Bank provided the loan, while a Walker & Dunlop team led by Aaron Appel, Dustin Stolly, Jonathan Schwartz, Keith Kurland, Adam Schwartz, Sean Reimer and Sean Bastian arranged the financing. “We’re pleased to once again partner with Legion, alongside SMA Equities, to arrange the financing that facilitated the acquisition of this irreplaceable Upper East Side condominium development site,” Appel said in a statement to CO. The assemblage at the corner of East 84th Street and Third Avenue has been nearly 20 years in the making, according to TRD. Samy Mahfar’s SMA Equities first purchased the corner lot at 1491-1493 Third Avenue in 2007, paying $33.8 million for the historic commercial building alongside real estate investor David Moussazadeh and Rex Properties’ Francis Moezinia. In 2016, the three partners secured the taller commercial property at 1495 Third Avenue next door for $18.2 million, according to city reports, and snapped up the five-story mixed-use apartment building at 1497 Third Avenue for $12.5 million in 2025. Demolition for the residential development is already underway, with Hill West Architects selected for its design. The forthcoming 510-foot-tall tower will include roughly 120 condos, according to New York YIMBY, and will offer 18,994 square feet of lower-level commercial space. The project with SMA Equities adds another feather to the cap of Legion’s Upper East Side portfolio, which includes luxury condominium towers at 109 East 79th Street and 1122 Madison Avenue. The latter development with Nahla Capital topped out in January. This past summer, Legion also wrapped vertical construction
bullets: Legion & SMA Equities secured $99M pre-dev loan, Upper East Side, 300K SF residential, 37-story tower
Site: 1491–1497 Third Ave. (corner 84th St.); assemblage nearly 20 years in the making
BDT & MSD Partners, Deutsche Bank financed; Walker & Dunlop arranged; SMA acquired corner lot in 2007
stories.summary: Legion Investment Group and SMA Equities secured a $99 million pre-development loan from BDT & MSD Partners and Deutsche Bank for a 300,000-square-foot, 37-story residential development at the corner of Third Avenue and East 84th Street on Manhattan's Upper East Side. The assemblage was nearly 20 years in the making, with SMA Equities having first purchased the corner lot in 2007 for $33.8 million. Walker & Dunlop arranged the financing.
stories.impact: Large-scale pre-dev financing for iconic Manhattan UES residential tower and successful long-hold land-assembly reflects strong institutional capital appetite and conviction in luxury residential fundamentals. Pre-dev financing availability at this scale indicates capital markets have stabilized post-2023 rate shock; multifamily developers should expect continued but selective access to leverage for core markets and established sponsors. Monitor comparable UES/Midtown assemblages for similar financing announcements.

stories.title: Harbor Associates Sells Office Campus in North L.A. County for $32M
stories.excerpt: Strauss Investments has acquired a smaller two-building office campus in northern Los Angeles County for $32 million. The San Diego-based investor purchased Commons at Valencia, a 157,189-square-foot Class A office property in Santa Clarita’s Valencia neighborhood from Harbor Associates, according to CBRE, which represented the seller. The deal is equal to about $204 per square foot. Commons at Valencia spans nearly 9 acres at 25124 and 25152 Springfield Court, just off Interstate 5, in Valencia in the Santa Clarita Valley. It includes two three-story buildings and a two-story parking structure with 625 spaces. The campus, built in 2005, is 79 percent leased with tenants in professional services, insurance, financial services and real estate industries. Harbor completed an extensive renovation in 2020. “Commons at Valencia attracted significant investor interest due to its strong tenant roster, recent capital improvements and strategic location within one of Southern California’s premier suburban office markets,” CBRE Senior Vice President Mark Shaffer said in a statement. “The property’s leasing momentum and long-term growth prospects within the Valencia submarket created a compelling investment opportunity for the buyer.” Shaffer represented Harbor in the sale alongside CBRE’s Anthony DeLorenzo, Sean Sullivan and Gerard Poutier. Valencia has remained one of the stronger-performing office submarkets in north L.A. County, according to CBRE, with persistent growth in its residential and employment bases. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Strauss Investments purchased Commons at Valencia, Santa Clarita CA, $32M ($204/SF)
157.2K SF Class A office campus (2 buildings, 9 acres), built 2005, 79% leased
Tenants: professional services, insurance, financial services, real estate; recent 2020 capital renovation
stories.summary: San Diego-based Strauss Investments acquired Commons at Valencia, a 157,189-square-foot Class A office campus in Santa Clarita's Valencia neighborhood, for $32 million ($204 per square foot). The campus includes two three-story buildings on 9 acres and was built in 2005 with extensive renovations completed in 2020. It is currently 79 percent leased to tenants in professional services, insurance, financial services, and real estate.
stories.impact: Suburban Los Angeles County office acquisition by regional investor signals stable but non-growth demand for satellite office space outside central LA; $204/SF pricing reflects weak cap-rate compression. Minimal direct signal for multifamily, though Santa Clarita's continued office tenancy supports employed renter base; developer focus should remain on core West LA/Santa Monica and emerging Inland Empire submarkets, not Santa Clarita office-adjacent residential.
